messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the allocator offload RFC — we need to nail tenant-fence semantics for cross-pool evictions. hitting a recurring OOM scenario in dedicated pools.
aneesh: can you paste a short repro? not sure I follow the exact gap.
maria: repro: tenant pins weights on dedicated pool, evictor tries to reclaim cold pages -> we start migration to host staging, but tenant-level lease prevents migration so pages stay resident and we OOM the pool.
kelly: proposed surface: `soft_fence(alloc_id, grace_ms)` -> returns `fence_token` or `deferred`; `finalize_fence(fence_token)` to actually free. Allows tenant agent to drain cache and checkpoint.
aneesh: two obvious worries: latency (we can't stall in-path inference) and correctness if tenant agent crashes/restarts and reclaims allocation mid-handshake. idempotency is critical.
sam: my thought: use a lease-versioning + soft-fence state. soft-fence marks pages as reclaimable (reads allowed), runtime migrates in background. if tenant reclaims, increment lease version and soft-fence fails fast. final fence requires matching lease version.
maria: that covers correctness. also want metrics: `fence_issued`, `fence_fail_reclaimed`, `fence_wait_ms` so we can tune grace windows.
kelly: handshake sketch (pseudo):
```
1) evictor -> soft_fence(alloc) // mark reclaimable, emit fence_token
2) tenant_agent -> drain_kvcache(alloc, timeout) // best-effort, returns ack or timeout
3) evictor -> attempt_migrate(alloc) // background migrate to staging/swap
4) evictor -> finalize_fence(fence_token) // validate lease_version, free pages
```
aneesh: fallback plan: if drain times out, escalate to demote_to_swap with limited window, then hard_fence after another timeout. must document expected SLOs.
evict-bot: note: pushed branch `mem-handshake-v4` with soft_fence API stub and telemetry counters.
sam: I'll prototype token layout: `tenant_id:alloc_id:lease_epoch:nonce` and ensure HMAC-signed for router trust. also will add API for checking token validity.
maria: also, Dedicated vs Hosted policy: Dedicated tenants should get longer default grace and opt-out to aggressive demotion. Hosted default remains conservative to protect node SLOs.
kelly: SGTM. i'll draft a 1-pager (design + state model + telemetry) and loop in eng-sre + runtime tomorrow 09:00 PST. :calendar:
maria: thanks — filing follow-up issue #4321 for implementation tasks and test plan.
aneesh: one more ask: add a chaos test that simulates tenant-agent crash during soft_fence to validate idempotency and fallback.
kelly: good call, will add to the test matrix.
maria: ok resolving for now, will link RFC follow-up in PR.
